nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: The main Express application entry point that sets up middleware (CORS, JSON parsing, cookies), registers all route handlers, initializes Socket.IO for real-time communication, and connects to the database before starting the HTTP server.

nodes.name: database.js
nodes.summary: A simple module that establishes a MongoDB connection using Mongoose with the connection string from environment variables, exported as an async function called by the app on startup.

nodes.name: auth.js
nodes.summary: An authentication middleware that validates a JWT token from the request cookie, looks up the corresponding user in the database, and attaches the user object to the request before passing control to the next handler.

nodes.name: chat.js
nodes.summary: Defines the Mongoose schemas and model for chat data, with a Chat document storing an array of participant user references and an array of timestamped messages each tied to a sender.

nodes.name: connectionRequest.js
nodes.summary: Defines the Mongoose model for connection requests between users, enforcing a status enum of ignored, interested, accepted, or rejected, and includes a pre-save validation to prevent users from sending requests to themselves.

nodes.name: payment.js
nodes.summary: Defines the Mongoose model for storing payment records, capturing Razorpay order and payment IDs, status, amount, currency, receipt, and membership-related notes linked to a user.

nodes.name: user.js
nodes.summary: Defines the Mongoose user schema with fields for profile info, credentials, and membership status, including email and URL validation via the validator library and bcrypt password hashing — the file appears to be truncated before the JWT method implementations.

nodes.name: auth.js
nodes.summary: Defines Express routes for user authentication — signup (validates input, hashes password, creates user, sets JWT cookie), login (verifies credentials, sets JWT cookie), and logout (clears the token cookie) — though the file appears truncated at the module.exports line.

nodes.name: chat.js
nodes.summary: Defines a GET endpoint that retrieves an existing chat conversation between the authenticated user and a target user by their ID, or creates a new empty chat if none exists, returning the chat with sender names populated.

nodes.name: payment.js
nodes.summary: Handles Razorpay payment integration with two endpoints: one to create a new membership payment order (silver or gold) and save it to the database, and a webhook endpoint to receive and validate payment status updates from Razorpay.

nodes.name: profile.js
nodes.summary: Provides two authenticated endpoints for user profile management: a GET route to view the currently logged-in user's profile, and a PATCH route to update editable profile fields after validating the request body.

nodes.name: request.js
nodes.summary: Manages friend/connection requests between users, exposing a POST endpoint that lets an authenticated user send an 'interested' or 'ignored' status request to another user while preventing duplicate requests.

nodes.name: user.js
nodes.summary: Exposes endpoints for social graph features including fetching pending incoming connection requests, listing all accepted connections, and providing a paginated feed of users the logged-in user has not yet interacted with.

nodes.name: constants.js
nodes.summary: Defines and exports a simple lookup object mapping membership tier names (silver, gold) to their corresponding prices in INR, used by the payment route.

nodes.name: cronjob.js
nodes.summary: Schedules a daily cron job at 8 AM that queries for all connection requests with 'interested' status created the previous day and sends a reminder email to each recipient who has pending requests.

nodes.name: razorpay.js
nodes.summary: Initializes and exports a singleton Razorpay SDK instance configured with API credentials from environment variables, used by the payment routes to create and manage orders.

nodes.name: sendEmail.js
nodes.summary: Provides a utility function to send HTML emails via AWS SES, hardcoding the sender and recipient addresses while accepting a subject and body as parameters. It wraps the SES SendEmailCommand and handles MessageRejected errors gracefully.

nodes.name: sesClient.js
nodes.summary: Creates and exports a configured AWS SES client instance targeting the ap-south-1 region, using AWS credentials loaded from environment variables.

nodes.name: socket.js
nodes.summary: Initializes a Socket.IO server that handles real-time chat functionality, including joining private rooms (identified by a hashed combination of two user IDs) and persisting sent messages to a MongoDB Chat collection before broadcasting them to room participants.

nodes.name: validation.js
nodes.summary: Exports two validation helper functions: one that validates required sign-up fields including email format and password strength, and another that checks whether profile edit requests only contain permitted fields.
